thread:
Maya: Noticed the live canary flipped between primary and fallback repeatedly on us (approx every 6-8s). Appears tied to rapid model_cache_miss spikes.
Diego: Saw crash logs from the cache layer then a spill of 502s. Router reacted immediately and flipped.
Priya: Can we design a small cooldown + hysteresis in the rollout policy instead of putting logic into the router? That keeps decisioning auditable.
Maya: Yes — policy-level cooldown also simplifies private installs because the policy snapshot travels with the decision.
Diego: Sketch: require N events in W seconds to trigger, and M good events in V seconds to recover. Add debounce_ms to suppress flapping within a short interval.
Priya: Proto sketch we used in testing:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "af_policy_2026",
  "triggers": [{"signal":"5xx","count":4,"window_sec":12}],
  "recover": {"count":12,"window_sec":40},
  "debounce_ms": 2000,
  "buffer_retention_sec": 30
}
```
Maya: UX: rollout card should show active variant + small reason pill. Clicking expands a timeline with the buffered events and a link to the policy snapshot id.
Diego: Telemetry: emit counters fallback.triggered{reason,policy} and fallback.buffer_count. Also include snapshot_hash tag for correlating to audit logs.
Priya: Implementation note: use a tiny ring buffer per-route (compressed tuples) with TTL. Expose only last 30s on console by default.
ops-bot: Incident I-2026-777 created by Diego  P2. Trace: https://internal/trace/I-2026-777
deploy-bot: Routing canary with ring-buffer export scheduled to staging at 1736004480.
Maya: Action items: Diego wires ring buffer and emits metrics, Priya drafts the policy proto + RFC, I'll mock the rollout flyout and attach a sim button for dry-run. Target: prototype in staging by EOD Friday.
